name: Alfonso VI Captures Toledo
summary: Alfonso VI of León-Castile captured Toledo in 1085, the ancient Visigothic capital that had been under Muslim rule for 373 years. The fall shocked the taifa kingdoms of al-Andalus, who collectively invited the Almoravid dynasty from Morocco to intervene. Toledo's fall was also culturally transformative: its libraries made Arabic philosophical and scientific texts accessible to Latin scholars, sparking the 12th-century translation movement.
outcomes: Ancient Visigothic capital recovered for Christianity
Almoravid intervention invited from North Africa
Toledo becomes center of translation movement

_quarry.structural_significance: The most symbolically significant victory of the Reconquista before Granada; Toledo's capture and its intellectual legacy reshaped both the political and cultural map of medieval Iberia.

sources_used: Reilly, The Kingdom of León-Castilla under King Alfonso VI
Burnett, The Introduction of Arabic Learning into England
